SFMTA 的“长者免费坐 Muni”（Free Muni for Senior: SFMTA's Free Muni for Seniors gives San Francisco residents 65+ with gross family income at or below 100% of Bay Area median free Muni rides, cable cars included, on a Clipper card. Applying online is fastest: enter your registered Senior Clipper card's serial number, or upload proof of age if you don't have one. You can also download the application in Chinese and mail or drop it off at the SFMTA Customer Service Center (11 South Van Ness Avenue, ATTN: FREE MUNI). Approval takes up to 3 weeks with an existing Clipper card and up to 4 weeks if a new card is needed.

65 岁以下有残障：Clipper Access 卡（原名 RTC）: Under 65 with a disability: Clipper Access (formerly RTC)
Clipper Access 是给 65 岁以下、有符合条件残障的乘客办的优惠卡: Clipper Access is the discount card for riders under 65 with qualifying disabilities, also 62.5% off BART. There are two paths: Basic eligibility (for example a Medicare card held by someone under 65, a DMV placard registration receipt, or existing ADA paratransit eligibility) and Medical eligibility (certified by a California licensed professional). When you apply, transit agency staff photocopy your documents and take your photo. Elders 65 and over simply get a Senior card.

In San Francisco it's SF Paratransit: general questions 415.351.7000 (Monday–Friday 9 a.m.–4:45 p.m.), SF Access reservations 415.285.6945, option 2 (daily 7 a.m.–6 p.m.). In the East Bay it's East Bay Paratransit, run by AC Transit and BART: (510) 287-5000, during AC Transit and BART operating hours, within ¾ mile of a bus route or BART station, with a rider guide in Chinese on its site. In other counties, ask the local transit agency's paratransit office.
